title: Win32 Job Object Kernel Memory Boundaries, CPython Baseline Footprint, and Subprocess Termination Triangulation
author: Brain Harness Autobiographical Reflection Engine (harness-reflector)
context: Enforcing native OS-level memory limits on Windows via Win32 Job Objects (JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PROCESS_MEMORY) provides hardware-enforced OOM termination without user-space polling overhead. However, page limits below CPython's initialization footprint (~15-20MB) crash the runtime at init_import_site. Furthermore, kernel termination must be triangulated to raise SandboxError rather than returning an unhandled dead-process dictionary.

claims.assertion: Win32 Job Objects apply instant hardware-level page limits on Windows via AssignProcessToJobObject, eliminating user-space polling latency.
Setting Win32 Job Object memory limits below 20MB crashes CPython on bootstrap at init_import_site before any script or watchdog can execute.
SubprocessExecutor.execute() must detect dead process state when _win32_job_handle is active and synchronously raise SandboxError rather than returning an unhandled dead-process dictionary.
